title: Request Dissector Workbench: unified debugging workspace for failed requests
creator: Avery Morales
description: Design a consolidated "Request Dissector" workspace inside Redwood Console focused on rapid error analysis and developer debugging workflows. The workbench combines a request-level timeline, retry/hop visualization, parsed payload inspector (JSON + non-JSON heuristics), error taxonomy ribbons, token-level latency markers, and quick actions (replay, export request, attach to evaluation). Goal: reduce MTTR for production LLM failures and make root-cause signals discoverable without deep infra knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Workbench UI surfaces a per-request timeline with retry hops and clear markers for 'first error' and 'final failure'
AC2: Payload inspector can switch between raw, parsed (JSON tree), and truncated-compact views and highlights fields referenced in model prompts
AC3: Error taxonomy tags (client | model | infra | policy | network) are suggested automatically and editable by the user
AC4: Quick actions menu provides Replay (sandboxed), Export (ndjson), Create Eval (link to eval harness), and Annotate (adds note to request) and respects RBAC
AC5: Console shows cost and token breakdown for the failed request inline and includes suggestion to rerun with a lower-context model variant
AC6: Accessibility: keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels implemented for timeline and inspector panels
AC7: Developer handoff includes annotated Figma protos, component spec, and API contract for request payload endpoints
activities: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with PM and Engineering (Sophie Kramer) to align on scope and metrics (MTTR, repro rate)
2025-02-15: Design spike — exploration of linear timeline vs stacked swimlane visualization; picked swimlane + condensed token markers after 2 prototypes
2025-02-20: Prototype v1 created in Figma (link below). Focus on timeline, retry hops, and quick actions flow
2025-02-22: Internal design critique with Ethan Brooks — prioritized payload parsing and error taxonomy discoverability
2025-02-26: UX review with PM (Luca Patel) and Observability lead — request-level cost signal added to header
2025-02-28: Developer sync — clarified API needs: request events stream, KV-cache keys, and retry metadata; ENG asked for pagination strategy
2025-03-01: Usability tests (3 sessions) with 2 platform SREs and 1 product engineer; key pain: noisy stacks when model errors bubble
2025-03-03: Updated prototype addressing feedback (compact stack traces, error group suggestions); preparing dev handoff artifacts
decision_log: Decisions: 1) Use swimlane timeline to show parallel retries and model fallback hops. 2) Restrict quick replay to users with 'playback' permission and route replays to a sandboxed tenant. 3) Error taxonomy will default to five buckets (client, infra, model, policy, network) with option to add custom tags. 4) Do not inline full token-level stack traces by default; reveal on demand to reduce noise.
reviewer_feedback: PM Luca Patel: emphasize cost signal and make 'suggested fix' actionable (link to run with different model variant)
Eng Sophie Kramer: need API contract for request event stream; prefetched KV cache keys would be very helpful for root cause correlation
Design Director Ethan Brooks: prefer smaller default footprint; timeline should not push critical logs below the fold
SRE Jordan Lee: add option to collapse noisy model stacks and show error group summaries
implementation_notes: Expose an events /requests/{id}/timeline endpoint returning an ordered list of events (timestamps, type, metadata) — ENG-9702 owns schema
Frontend: implement lazy-rendering for token-level views to keep initial load < 300ms
Backend: add indexing for request->retry chain and precompute error-group suggestions using heuristics in ENG-9810
Rollout: feature-flagged to 10% of orgs, then gated by supported runtime versions
next_steps: Finalize annotated Figma screens and component spec (Due 2025-03-05)
Create GH issue with API contract and sample payloads (ENG-9702)
Schedule follow-up usability test after dev alpha (target 2025-04-01)
